Topics · One God, one message

What about people who never heard the message?

None is held to a message that never reached them. No burden beyond capacity, no good lost, the verdict God's.

Part 1 of 3

﴿مَّنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَهْتَدِى لِنَفْسِهِۦ ۖ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيْهَا ۚ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ ۗ وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his soul. And whoever errs only errs against it. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And never would We punish until We sent a messenger.

Quran · Al-Isra 17:15

Translation

For each man will bear his own burden.

Original · Ancient Greek

ἕκαστος γὰρ τὸ ἴδιον φορτίον βαστάσει.

Galatians · 6:5

World English Bible

The question tests God's own justice: how can anyone be held to what they never knew? The answer begins from a principle every fair mind accepts: no one is charged under a law never announced. The verse places that principle on God Himself: He does not punish until a messenger has been sent. On this book's own words, God binds Himself by what you already know of justice. Whoever truly never received the message is not charged with refusing it.

A question for you

Who is on your mind as you ask this?

If you sayMy family or ancestors
ThenThat is a question of love. The verse gives you a principle you can rest on, and the verdict on each person stays with the One who truly knows them.
If you sayFar-off peoples of the world
Then16:36 said every nation had a messenger, so the question is wider than it looks. Then there are those who received a distorted account, and that comes next.
If you sayPeople who heard and are not convinced
ThenA different question, with its own place: if I am sincerely mistaken, am I still responsible?

Part 2 of 3

﴿لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا ۚ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ ۗ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا ۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَآ إِصْرًا كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِنَا ۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِۦ ۖ وَٱعْفُ عَنَّا وَٱغْفِرْ لَنَا وَٱرْحَمْنَآ ۚ أَنتَ مَوْلَىٰنَا فَٱنصُرْنَا عَلَى ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْكَـٰفِرِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Allāh does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what [good] it has gained, and it will bear [the consequence of] what [evil] it has earned. "Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people."[111]

Translator's notes

[111] Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) concludes this sūrah by directing His servants how to supplicate Him, just as He taught them in Sūrah al-Fātiḥah how to praise Him and ask for guidance.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:286

Translation

For if the readiness is there, it is acceptable according to what you have, not according to what you don’t have.

Original · Ancient Greek

εἰ γὰρ ἡ προθυμία πρόκειται, καθὸ ἐὰν ἔχῃ εὐπρόσδεκτος, οὐ καθὸ οὐκ ἔχει.

2 Corinthians · 8:12

World English Bible

﴿إِلَّا ٱلْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ وَٱلنِّسَآءِ وَٱلْوِلْدَٰنِ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ حِيلَةً وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ سَبِيلًا٩٨ فَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَعْفُوَ عَنْهُمْ ۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَفُوًّا غَفُورًا٩٩﴾

Translation of the meaning

Except for the oppressed among men, women and children who cannot devise a plan nor are they directed to a way[213] - For those it is expected that Allāh will pardon them, and Allāh is ever Pardoning[214] and Forgiving.

Translator's notes

[213] They are prevented by circumstances beyond their control.

[214] Refer to footnote in 4:43.

Quran · An-Nisa 4:98-99

Many people, though, have heard something that hardly resembles the message: a distorted picture, or one carried by someone who harmed them. The wider rule is the first verse: no soul is asked beyond its capacity. Justice looks at ability, not at the outward case. The second, on those unable to leave a place of oppression, speaks of men, women and children who could find no means and no way. Real inability counts with God, and none of us can assess another's.

A question for you

What can keep a person from truly hearing the message, even when its words reached them?

If you sayWhoever carried it badly
ThenThat lays a heavy duty on anyone who carries a message, and points to the manner 16:125 calls for.
If you sayUpbringing and surroundings
ThenThat is real, and the fine question is what still remains to the person after it.
If you sayNothing, everyone is able
ThenThen you count inability as rare. The verse allows for it, and leaves the assessing to God, not to you or anyone.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَمَا يَفْعَلُوا۟ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَلَن يُكْفَرُوهُ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌۢ بِٱلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And whatever good they do - never will it be denied them. And Allāh is Knowing of the righteous.

Quran · Aal Imran 3:115

﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلصَّـٰبِـِٔينَ وَٱلنَّصَـٰرَىٰ وَٱلْمَجُوسَ وَٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَـٰمَةِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ شَهِيدٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Indeed, those who have believed and those who were Jews and the Sabeans and the Christians and the Magians and those who associated with Allāh - Allāh will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed Allāh is, over all things, Witness.[919]

Translator's notes

[919] See footnote of 4:79.

Quran · Al-Hajj 22:17

Translation

Then you shall return and discern between the righteous and the wicked, between him who serves God and him who doesn’t serve him.

Original · Hebrew

וְשַׁבְתֶּם֙ וּרְאִיתֶ֔ם בֵּ֥ין צַדִּ֖יק לְרָשָׁ֑ע בֵּ֚ין עֹבֵ֣ד אֱלֹהִ֔ים לַאֲשֶׁ֖ר לֹ֥א עֲבָדֽוֹ׃

Malachi · 3:18

World English Bible

The hardest question remains: what of one particular person? The honest answer is that we are not asked to know. The first verse says no good deed is lost. The second lists the faiths, Muslims among them, and says God will decide between them on the Day. The verdict is given to no group. That does not make all claims equal. It means none of us sits in that seat.

The same in the other books

Give alms from your possessions. When you give alms, don’t let your eye be envious. Don’t turn away your face from any poor man, and the face of God won’t be turned away from you. As your possessions are, give alms of it according to your abundance. If you have little, don’t be afraid to give alms according to that little; for you lay up a good treasure for yourself against the day of necessity;
